notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

The CPU undervolt tuner no longer fails boost steps for the voltage limit. On a console whose
Max voltage is at or under its voltage cap, every boost step was failed as "rail cap" at the
2703 MHz test, so the tuner kept the mildest boost step. If your result shows boost step 1,
run the CPU undervolt tuner again. First runs on Mariko consoles now start at normal step 7
and boost step 9, where most consoles land, instead of climbing from the bottom; a step a
console cannot hold steps back down on its own.

Retro Rewind now checks for updates against the Retro Rewind team's own update list and
installs their small update packages, so 6.13.1 (28 MB) installs, where the full download
still gives 6.13.0. Mario Kart Wii's menu shows the version you have, an Update row when a
newer one is out, and a Rebuild row only when an update changes the game's code; an update
that only adds tracks, sounds or menus plays right away.

Wii U games kept as disc images (.wux or .wud) now show their title ID once their disc key
is added, so their shader caches can be uploaded and cleared, and graphic packs match them.

The pause menu now opens in your colors, with every row, from its first frame. Saving or
loading a 3DS state no longer shows the game over the menu or plays its sound. The 3DS
screen layout is now a list to pick from, applied while the game stays paused. Quitting a
3DS, GameCube, Wii or PS2 game no longer shows the emulator's window on the way out.

PC games that answer Quit with a box of their own, like Dead Space's "are you sure", are
ended and remembered, and their next quit skips the box. Each PC game has a new "When you
quit" option for this.

Settings now scrolls at a steady 60 fps; the Display and Sound pages scrolled at 20 to 30.

The first quit of a game like Dead Space still shows its box for about a second. The tuner
fix was tested on one console, and the new starting steps have not run on a console yet.
Quitting with the controller's quit hotkey still shows the emulator's window.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
